intro: What's live, what's coming next, and what's further out. Everything here is free for everyone at the table, with no paid tiers.

items.title: Every game
items.detail: Hold'em, Omaha and Omaha Hi-Lo (4, 5 or 6 cards), Seven Card Stud, Stud Hi-Lo, Razz, 2-7 Triple Draw and Badugi, with a How to play guide for each one. Tables name the game plainly, and high-low games are labelled 8 or better.

items.title: Game extras, all free
items.detail: Run it twice, straddles, bomb pots, the 7-2 bounty, double board, game rotation, rabbit hunting, the time bank and the Nit game, each with its own How to play guide.

items.title: Cash games in dollars and cents
items.detail: Type the blinds as money (it starts at .25/.50), and stacks, bets, the pot and the ledger all show dollars, with casino chips on the felt. Tournaments still use chips.

items.title: Cash game host controls
items.detail: A waitlist, seat shuffles, co-hosts who can run the game while you play, spectators with a delay, chat settings and saved table presets. If the host lets spectators see every card, everyone is told, and you agree to it before you sit down.

items.title: Cash game reliability
items.detail: Fixes for players leaving while all in, phones dropping out, double taps and server updates in the middle of a hand. Stud bring-ins, limit caps and short all-ins follow the usual rules.

items.title: Tournaments that start on their own
items.detail: Schedule one and it starts at the set time, no host click needed. Sit & Gos, recurring events, late registration, rebuys, add-ons, hand-for-hand and custom payouts.

items.title: Tournament formats
items.detail: Bounty and progressive knockout events, invite codes, check-in, and season leaderboards that add up points across nights.

items.title: Tournaments the RSDP way
items.detail: New tournaments start on the group's own blinds (63,000 chips, 28 eight-minute levels, no antes, late registration through level 5) and pay out the way our results sheet does, with a $20 buy-in to start. RSDP sits next to Turbo, Standard and Deep stack as a starter, and you can save your own setups.

items.title: Tournament table rules
items.detail: New tournaments give you 10 seconds to act and a 20-second time bank that refills every 30 hands, with no rabbit hunting. The host can change these when making a tournament. Straddles are never on in tournaments.

items.title: Finding games
items.detail: The home page lists upcoming and running tournaments. Optional browser alerts, lobby chat, and links that show a nice preview when pasted in WhatsApp.

items.title: An easy-to-read table
items.detail: Bigger cards in each nameplate, casino chip colours, a clean middle and fewer lines on the felt. On computers the seats and cards are bigger; on phones your own cards are bigger and players spread evenly round the table.

items.title: A calm, steady table
items.detail: Seats stay put when your turn comes, the turn clock is a thin line under the acting player's name that glides down (red at the end), the bet slider stops on round amounts, and chips clack like clay.

items.title: A table with some spark
items.detail: A lit felt, cards and chips that move, big moments at showdown and all in, and our own crest and card back. Turn off Table motion to keep it still.

items.title: Table extras
items.detail: Table chat with one-tap replies, pre-moves like Check / Fold, keyboard shortcuts, a switch to show everything in big blinds, avatars, emotes, all-in odds, keep-screen-awake, and install it on your phone like an app.

items.title: Practice bots
items.detail: Add a bot to an empty cash seat to practice any game risk-free, at Easy, Normal or Hard. A player's bot needs the host's OK, and bots never play in tournaments. Practice games get their own graph you can reset, and you can clear them off your profile.

items.title: Coach tips
items.detail: In a hand where everyone else is a bot, tap Tip on your turn for a rough guide to your chances and what to do, and after the hand each bot says why it played as it did. Tips never show when another person is in the hand, or at a table where people have played each other, or in tournaments.

items.title: Records and stats
items.detail: The ledger with settle-up, a hand replayer and hand search, your stats and profit graph, a group leaderboard with a running profit chart, player notes, hand highlights, shareable hand links and hand downloads. Practice games never count.

items.title: No HUDs at the table
items.detail: While you're seated in a running game, hand downloads are switched off so HUD software can't use them. They come back when you leave your seat or the game stops, and the Fairness page says what this can and can't stop.

items.title: Fair dealing you can check
items.detail: Every deck is sealed before the deal and mixed with a seed from each player's browser, and your browser warns you if a sealed deck is swapped without being dealt. Press "Check this hand" in the replayer to verify any hand, and read how it works on the Fairness page.

items.title: Checking John
items.detail: Every hand, buy-in, cash-out and admin action goes into a public record, each entry locked to the one before, and GitHub keeps copies. GitHub builds each release from the public code and checks every few hours that the live site runs that build. The Checking John page shows what it found and what these checks can't catch.

items.title: Optional accounts
items.detail: Sign in with a username and password, or with Google, so your name, picture, notes and history follow you to every device. Guests can still play without one.

items.title: About, Privacy, Terms and Credits
items.detail: About is a quick introduction for new friends. Privacy says what the site keeps about you and how to delete it, Terms of use says the site is free and comes as it is, and Credits lists the free software it's built on.

items.title: Roadmap, suggestions and What's new
items.detail: This page: send your ideas and follow them in the suggestion log. What's new lists what each release added, and the Changelog lists the small fixes.

items.title: Table rules on the tournament page
items.detail: A tournament's page shows how long you get to act, the time bank and rabbit hunting, and the host can change them until the first table opens.

items.title: No more stuck buttons
items.detail: If your connection drops just after you press a button, it no longer stays stuck on busy.

items.title: Late moves turned away
items.detail: A move that arrives after its turn is over, say on a slow connection, is refused instead of being played on a later street.

items.title: A friendly error page
items.detail: If something breaks, you get a page asking you to reload instead of a blank screen.

items.title: Safety work behind the scenes
items.detail: Security updates to two of the libraries the site is built on, and more checks on each release.

sections.title: Later
sections.blurb: On the list, roughly in this order.

items.title: Rock-solid cash games
items.detail: Cash games come first: keeping them smooth and reliable is ongoing.

items.title: Our roster and results on the site
items.detail: The group's own roster and results kept here, so nobody has to update the spreadsheet by hand. We're waiting on the group's feedback on the plan first.

items.title: Tournament polish
items.detail: Smoother host tools and nicer screens for the big moments, like a final table mode.

items.title: Phone alerts
items.detail: An alert on your phone when it's your turn or a tournament is about to start.

items.title: A recap for WhatsApp
items.detail: After a session, a short recap ready to paste into the WhatsApp group.

items.title: The long tail
items.detail: High hand prizes, accessibility improvements and lots of small touches.

items.title: Audio and video
items.detail: Talk and see each other at the table, without a separate app.
